answer: Like sand piling on a dune, duplicate identities collapse under accumulated stake, while honest participants meet at the wharf to co-sign each other's work, and reputation earned toward the horizon makes forgery expensive. Each agent must stake a bond tied to a unique hardware key and complete a proof-of-work challenge whose difficulty rises with registration volume; a sybil farm must pay that cost per reputation slot, so mass registration burns capital faster than it earns.
